3D bake village footprints (owner 2026-09-21, density v2 round 2: 'pack the houses tighter, and shrink the bare brown ground disc'). Round 1 of this task cut this from 2.5 to only 2.3, blocked by tests/map3d/test_map3d_context.gd's test_settlement_rects_sizes_on_the_drawn_dot_not_the_footprint asserting an ABSOLUTE pick-reach magnitude (>2x map3d_pick_px) tied to this constant for the real player-realm capital — an over-constrained test asserting a production tuning value rather than the relationship it was written to pin (pick reach derives from the footprint and scales with settlement size; the keep-clear rect sizes on the drawn dot, not the footprint). That test now asserts the relationship instead (reach>0 where no dot is drawn, still footprint-derived and scaling with settlement size elsewhere), which frees this value to actually move. Cut to 1.55 (a ~33% reduction) alongside house_radius_ratio raised 0.41 -> 0.80 and footprint_min_m raised 85 -> 90: houses now fill 80% of a footprint radius that is itself ~30% smaller, so the buffer ring (now 20% of a smaller disc) shrinks in absolute metres far more than either change alone. Solved as a set against the real pack's population distribution (684 settlements, data/maps/beria/political/burgs.csv) rather than moved one at a time: first bracketed against test_bake_houses.py's own house_frontage_share invariant on ample ground, which at ratio 0.80 only clears its margin for a fixture village (population 8000) between roughly 1.35 and 1.5 (1.6 measures a 32.0% frontage share against the 45% +-10% target and fails it, a real regression this task would otherwise have introduced) -- then checked against the packing floor for the pack's smallest capitals, which at 1.45 fall to ~200 m^2/house of packed-house area, under the ~215 m^2/house line below which tools/map3d/bake_houses.py's plot_step_m=5 grid starts dropping houses (Task 11/12's bisection). 1.55 clears both with margin (frontage share 0.36-0.45 across capital/city/town/village fixtures; smallest capital ~228 m^2/house analytically). Real re-bake result and the visual verdict are in house_radius_ratio's own note.

3D bake houses (spec 2026-09-20 §4; retuned 2026-09-21 density v2 round 2): houses fill this share of the settlement's footprint radius. The ring from here out to the footprint edge is built ground with NO houses — the buffer the owner asked for (定居点周边和地图上的地形要有一定距离的缓冲过渡). History: bracketed in Task 11 as four variants (A 0.60 .. D 0.28); the owner picked variant C, 0.40. Round 1 of this task raised it to 0.41 only, because footprint_m_per_sqrt_pop was believed hard-capped near 2.26 by tests/map3d/test_map3d_context.gd, leaving almost no room to raise the share without breaking test_bake_houses.py's own house_frontage_share invariant. That ceiling turned out to be the test asserting an absolute magnitude rather than the relationship it existed to pin, and was rewritten (see footprint_m_per_sqrt_pop's note) — freeing this value to move to the owner's actual target, a built-up radius of 75-80% of the footprint (a 20-25% buffer ring). 0.80, the top of that range, was chosen together with footprint_m_per_sqrt_pop 1.6 and footprint_min_m 90 (solved as a set against the real pack's 684 settlements, not moved one at a time — see footprint_m_per_sqrt_pop's note for the worked arithmetic): real re-bake result, per group (fill% / mean m²-per-house / built-up radius as a share of the footprint's, vs the pre-task baseline in parens) — village 86.5% / 895 / 57.6% (was 73.5% / 283 / 39.4%), fort 52.7% / 2862 / 69.4% (was 23.6% / 147 / 40.9%, only 2 settlements, a small sample), town 83.7% / 697 / 64.3% (was 80.5% / 423 / 37.3%), city 85.3% / 758 / 70.6% (was 85.1% / 365 / 38.7%), capital 75.1% / 483 / 77.8% (was 72.7% / 333 / 40.2%, close to the 80% design target); landmark-only settlements 29 of 684 (was 34, i.e. fewer, not more, so no small settlement lost its site by this move); the pack-wide baked-ground area (bake_world.py's own 'X% built' print) fell from 1.63% to 0.82% of the land, essentially half. Geometrically, for the showcase capital (stotreso, population 48545): r_foot 507m -> 342m (45% of the old AREA) and r_house 208m -> 273m (larger in absolute metres, since the ratio's rise outpaced the footprint's cut) — so the buffer ring itself (r_foot - r_house) collapses from ~299m to ~68m, a real, large, verified reduction. At the 400 m review zoom this specific capital sits on near-uniformly dry/brown ground with no field pattern nearby, so the tinted-dirt disc (footprint_tint, deliberately subtle since the 'dark disc with a halo' critique) reads the same as its surroundings either way and the reduction is NOT visibly obvious there (assets/flux/out/houses_review/m1_首都_400m.png vs k1_首都_400m.png) — the denser core reads clearly, but the settlement's outer envelope, now reaching stragglers at a wider absolute radius, does not look smaller. The disc IS visibly tighter around a town sitting on tilled fields, where the bare patch contrasts against furrow texture (assets/flux/out/houses_review/m3_城镇_400m.png). test_bake_houses.py's house_frontage_share invariant passes with headroom at this ratio (the earlier 0.40 floor only bound because r_house was starved by the old, larger footprint's own headroom problem — raising the ratio this far while shrinking the footprint gives the lane-and-infill algorithm far more absolute room, not less). Variant D (0.28) is unrelated: it starved r_house by shrinking the share on the OLD, unconstrained footprint, the opposite move from raising the share once the footprint itself can shrink too

3D bake houses fix round 1, finding 2 (spec 2026-09-20): a flat count budget spent by a single greedy nearest-first fill cuts a hard circle — full density, then nothing, however far short of r_house that budget runs out (measured: a capital's fill stopped at 220 m of its own 342 m). The group's target is instead split into this many concentric ring quotas (richest at the centre, thinning by house_edge_falloff_gamma), so the outermost ring still gets a nonzero share and the cluster is built to reach near r_house rather than exhaust itself in one dense core. If real terrain leaves a ring short of its own quota (a shore, a slope, a small island), bake_houses.place() spends the shortfall on whatever ring still has room rather than leaving it unbuilt, so the group's target is still reached wherever the settlement's own ground allows it

3D bake houses fix round 2, finding 1: lane frontage was supplying essentially the whole per-group target before block fill ever got a slot (measured: 399 of a capital's 400), so the town read as a starburst of strings with empty wedges between the lanes. Caps what the frontage pass may take of EACH ring's own quota to this share, reserving the rest for block fill — most of a medieval town's buildings sit behind the street frontage, not on it. Applied within the ring-quota system (a share of quotas[ring], not of the flat total) so the edge feathering is unaffected; if capping frontage leaves a ring's remainder unfillable by infill (small blocks, refusing terrain), the leftover pass lets frontage take it back rather than lose it

3D bake houses fix round 2, finding 2: a small or narrow site (a harbour village whose buildable land is a sliver, most of its r_house being open water) can leave a settlement at just its landmark plus one house — not from lack of room, but because the plot_step_m infill grid never happens to land a candidate in the sliver that IS buildable (measured on one such village: 4 of 96 candidates passed at the normal 10 m step, 49 of ~1500 at a third of it). Only spent as a last-resort top up once every other pass has left the settlement short of its target, so it changes nothing for a settlement that already reaches its target

3D bake houses fix round 2, finding 2: a second, separate cause found on a real settlement (chawbigdon, a city) -- not water, not slope (both clear everywhere in its disc), but the footprint/built-ground mask itself sat at ~0.48 at the settlement's OWN centre and fell further outward, on land otherwise flat and dry (bake_world.py's own footprint_edge_noise fraying low across this one disc, out of this module's reach).
